COLDWAR_SYR_baath_01.description: The Regional Command can place provincial organisers and military appointments within a single chain of authority. A disciplined vanguard would assemble reserves and secure command resources more quickly. Its preference for political reliability will also narrow the space available to independent specialists and critical inquiry within the state.
COLDWAR_SYR_baath_01.reference: SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: mobilization +5%, planning +5%, training time -10%, terrain penalty reduction +10%. Syrian adaptation concentrates on party mobilization and command resources, with a research penalty.

COLDWAR_SYR_baath_02.description: Socialists, Communists and Arab nationalists can contribute workplace organisations and experienced administrators to a broader governing front. Binding their participation to public services and labour guarantees can make civilian production more dependable. Consultation will slow unilateral decisions, while the social commitments that sustain cooperation must receive continuing funding.
COLDWAR_SYR_baath_02.reference: PER_rials_behind_red_tape, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: civilian productivity +5%, political power +5%, bureaucracy costs -2%. PER_utilize_workers_house, cost 7.2: efficiency gain +10%, health and social costs -5% each. Syrian adaptation uses +5% civilian productivity with funded coalition obligations.

COLDWAR_SYR_hafez_01.description: Urban merchants retain capital, skilled managers and commercial connections that the presidency cannot create by decree. Reconciliation can bring that experience back into civilian production and help agreed investments reach completion sooner. Tax concessions and closer exposure to foreign markets are the price of restoring confidence without surrendering the state's socialist institutions.
COLDWAR_SYR_hafez_01.reference: PER_rials_behind_red_tape, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: civilian productivity +5%. Native MD receiving_investment_duration_modifier is read by 99_investment_scripted_effects.txt. Existing Syrian market exposure is preserved and remains consumed by mdcw_cold_war_effects.txt.

COLDWAR_SYR_hafez_02.description: Reliable intermediaries in the armed forces can give the presidency a coherent chain of command and officers prepared to carry out its orders. Patronage must nevertheless be maintained through appointments and military pay. A system that rewards personal loyalty will find it harder to retain specialists whose judgement challenges the men around the president.
COLDWAR_SYR_hafez_02.reference: Native Syrian 2000 SYR_peoples_army and SYR_loyal_elite are mutually exclusive institutional army programmes. SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3, supplies several military modifiers of 5-10%. Syrian adaptation chooses command cohesion over merchant-led growth, with real personnel expenditure.

COLDWAR_SYR_industry_01.description: Public factories carry the promises of the socialist transformation alongside worn equipment and confused responsibilities. Rehabilitating plant management and production schedules can raise civilian output while helping military manufacturers master their existing lines. The state will retain responsibility for the workers and welfare commitments attached to its enterprises.
COLDWAR_SYR_industry_01.reference: PER_rials_behind_red_tape, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: civilian productivity +5%. PER_utilize_workers_house, cost 7.2: factory efficiency gain +10%. Syrian adaptation halves the efficiency-gain bonus and adds a social-spending burden.

COLDWAR_SYR_industry_02.description: Aleppo and Damascus retain workshop traditions supported by merchants, accountants and trading houses. Giving regulated private manufacturers room to invest can accelerate civilian construction and strengthen the services that organise their business. Tax concessions reduce immediate receipts, while imported equipment and export customers expose the country more closely to external conditions.
COLDWAR_SYR_industry_02.reference: Native MD Iranian 2000 economic focuses use offices_productivity +5% and civilian productivity +5% bundles. Existing Syrian workshop construction, tax and market-exposure effects are retained in purpose; construction rises to 7% and office productivity is a distinct 4% reward.

COLDWAR_SYR_industry_06.description: Aleppo's textile producers connect cotton-growing districts with urban employment and foreign customers. Better machinery, dependable deliveries and common quality standards can strengthen civilian production along that chain. Public support must also provide for workers whose jobs and household security depend on the mills remaining open through changes in demand.
COLDWAR_SYR_industry_06.reference: PER_rials_behind_red_tape, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: civilian productivity +5%. Corrects the previous military factory-output modifier on a civilian textile programme; the Syrian adaptation gives civilian productivity +6% with social costs +2%.

COLDWAR_SYR_industry_08.description: Imported medicines leave hospitals vulnerable to interrupted deliveries and scarce foreign exchange. Laboratories, inspection services and pharmaceutical training in Damascus can reduce the cost of supplying the public health system. Reliable domestic production requires a continuing commitment to technical education and rigorous standards rather than protection for poorly made substitutes.
COLDWAR_SYR_industry_08.reference: PER_utilize_workers_house, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: health and social spending costs -5% each. Syrian pharmaceutical preparation provides a smaller health saving of 3%, offset by education spending +2%.

COLDWAR_SYR_industry_11.description: A pharmaceutical facility in the capital will give domestic medicine production a permanent industrial base. Local manufacturing can improve civilian output and make hospital supplies less costly to obtain. The government must continue training chemists and technicians so that the new plant delivers dependable medicines after the construction teams have departed.
COLDWAR_SYR_industry_11.reference: Preserves the existing once-only industrial complex in state 186 and all its control/capacity conditions. PER_rials_behind_red_tape supplies a civilian-productivity reference of +5%; PER_utilize_workers_house supplies a health-cost reference of -5%. Both Syrian medicine focuses together reduce health costs by 5%, not 8%.

one_time.code: add_doctrine_cost_reduction = { name = COLDWAR_SYR_army_03 category = land_doctrine cost_reduction = 0.25 uses = 1 }

COLDWAR_SYR_army_03.description: Staff officers must coordinate supply, read terrain and challenge a plan before soldiers pay for its mistakes. A serious staff college can prepare operational plans more quickly and turn the army's experience into doctrinal study. Maintaining qualified instructors will require a continuing educational budget and promotion standards that reward competence.
COLDWAR_SYR_army_03.reference: SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: planning +5%, mobilization +5%, training time -10%, terrain penalty reduction +10%. Native Syrian 2000 SYR_guerrilla_warfare and SYR_decentralised_tactics each cost 10 and grant one 50% land_doctrine cost reduction. Syrian 1970 uses a smaller one-use 25% reduction and planning +8%.

COLDWAR_SYR_army_06.description: A recoverable vehicle should not be abandoned because the right workshop or tow team is missing. Repair detachments and stocked maintenance depots can reduce equipment losses from wear and help restore damaged industrial facilities. Spare parts, tools and specialist workshops must receive a regular share of the equipment budget even when no new weapons are being purchased.
COLDWAR_SYR_army_06.reference: Native engine modifiers_documentation.md documents attrition and industry_repair_factor. Native MD 00_money_system.txt reads equipment_cost_multiplier_modifier into equipment expenditure. Values are Syrian balance adaptations: attrition -5%, repair speed +10%, equipment costs +2%; no repair of specific equipment is scripted or claimed.

COLDWAR_SYR_army_07.description: Reliable non-commissioned officers turn orders into action when officers cannot supervise every section and vehicle. Permanent training schools can prepare recruits more efficiently and help formations regain cohesion after exertion. Experienced instructors and longer serving NCOs will expect the pay and career prospects of a professional military occupation.
COLDWAR_SYR_army_07.reference: SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: training time -10%. Syrian NCO schools use -5% training time and native army_morale_factor +3% recovery; native MD personnel cost modifier +2% funds professional pay.

COLDWAR_SYR_army_09.description: Mobile reserves must reach a threatened sector before an opportunity disappears. Dedicated movement plans and rehearsed command procedures can shorten preparation and improve the army's ability to redeploy. Keeping transport and armoured formations ready for that role will increase fuel consumption whenever the army operates, including campaigns far from its preferred routes.
COLDWAR_SYR_army_09.reference: SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: planning +5% alongside other training benefits. Syrian reserve adaptation uses planning +8%, army speed +3%, army fuel consumption +4%, replacing another generic organization increment.

COLDWAR_SYR_army_10.description: Prepared defensive belts need surveyed positions, rehearsed work parties and stores placed where troops will use them. Engineering support can help formations entrench more quickly and improve the protection their positions can provide. Labour and materials reserved for these works will also slow the country's civilian construction programme.
COLDWAR_SYR_army_10.reference: Native engine modifiers_documentation.md documents dig_in_speed_factor and flat max_dig_in. Syrian balance adaptation: entrenchment speed +15%, maximum entrenchment +2 points, construction speed -1%; these are country-wide doctrine benefits, not free fort buildings.

COLDWAR_SYR_infrastructure_01.description: Interior towns and agricultural districts need reliable connections to the country's larger markets. Concentrating engineers on inland routes can accelerate infrastructure work and reduce waste in the army's distribution system. Communities asked to accommodate new roads and depots will require resettlement support and services that extend beyond the first construction season.
COLDWAR_SYR_infrastructure_01.reference: Replaces identical infrastructure_01/02 +3% infrastructure construction and +1.2% bureaucracy packages. Native Syrian army logistics already uses supply_consumption_factor -2%; the inland programme uses -3% alongside infrastructure construction +8% and social costs +2%. Country modifiers do not geographically restrict later construction to inland states.

COLDWAR_SYR_infrastructure_02.description: The coastal corridor links inland producers to shipping agents, imported machinery and foreign customers. Concentrating services around the ports can improve commercial administration and the productivity of civilian industry throughout their trading network. Projects serving this concentration will require a larger Syrian contribution when the government accepts outside investment.
COLDWAR_SYR_infrastructure_02.reference: Native main MD Iranian 2000 economy bundles use offices_productivity +5% and civilian productivity +5%. Syrian coast adaptation uses offices +6%, civilians +3%, receiving-investment cost +2%; it promises national network effects rather than an engine-enforced coastal bonus.

COLDWAR_SYR_great_powers_01.description: The cabinet can organise military schools and procurement offices around the Soviet equipment already familiar to Syrian forces. Common procedures make training and technical adaptation less costly. Dependence on one strategic relationship also gives foreign influence greater room within Syrian affairs; new Soviet aid or specialist missions will still require an agreement with Moscow.
COLDWAR_SYR_great_powers_01.reference: SOV_academy, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: training time -10%. Native engine equipment_upgrade_xp_cost applies to equipment-design experience costs. Native MD 00_influence_scripted_effects.txt reads target foreign_influence_defense_modifier; -3% reduces Syrian resistance. Positive foreign_influence_modifier would instead benefit Syrian influence abroad and is deliberately not used.

COLDWAR_SYR_great_powers_02.description: Procurement officers and commercial representatives can prepare Syria to work with several foreign partners. Better contract administration will help licensed production and agreed investments proceed more efficiently. The armed forces must nevertheless maintain incompatible equipment and separate stocks, increasing the demands on their supply network even when diversification widens the cabinet's diplomatic options.
COLDWAR_SYR_great_powers_02.reference: Native engine license_production_speed and native MD receiving_investment_duration_modifier are supported country effects; 99_investment_scripted_effects.txt consumes the investment-duration modifier. Syrian adaptation grants licensed production +10% and investment duration -10%, offset by supply consumption +2%. Foreign licences and investment still require their actual agreements.

COLDWAR_SYR_agriculture_13.description: Cotton can connect Syrian farms, textile mills and foreign buyers through a more dependable export programme. Concentrating extension services and purchasing arrangements on that crop can increase agricultural output and receipts. The government will also have to support households whose livelihoods become more dependent on the performance of a single commercial crop.
COLDWAR_SYR_agriculture_13.reference: PER_control_tax_evasion, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 5.72: agriculture district income-tax modifier +5%, population tax income +2.5%, interest multiplier -15%. Syrian cotton policy uses agriculture-tax receipts +4%, agricultural productivity +5%, social costs +3%; no commodity-specific engine output is invented.

COLDWAR_SYR_agriculture_14.description: A dependable domestic food supply can protect households and public relief budgets from interrupted imports. Extension services and purchasing priorities will favour staple production and local distribution. The treasury must accept less revenue from these protected channels in exchange for lower pressure on the social budget and a more reliable supply of essential food.
COLDWAR_SYR_agriculture_14.reference: PER_utilize_workers_house, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 7.2: social costs -5% alongside other benefits. Syrian food-security adaptation uses social costs -4%, agricultural productivity +4%, tax receipts -1%, creating a fiscal alternative to the cotton route rather than a weaker duplicate.

COLDWAR_SYR_navy_01.description: A small navy must make its limited forces work together if it is to threaten an opponent near Syria's coast. Rehearsed approaches, shared reporting and coordinated deployments can improve the fleet's position in battle. Maintaining that readiness requires fuel for training and patrols even when the government avoids a wider naval confrontation.
COLDWAR_SYR_navy_01.reference: SOV_roscosmos_intel, main MD 05_russia.txt, cost 3: naval coordination +5%, positioning +5%, plus land planning and reconnaissance +5% each. Syrian coastal-denial adaptation uses positioning +5%, coordination +3%, navy fuel consumption +2%, without granting ships.

COLDWAR_SYR_navy_02.description: Merchant traffic needs escorts able to keep station, share contact reports and reach threatened shipping before losses mount. Dedicated drills can improve convoy protection and the fleet's ability to move between assignments. Longer escort commitments will consume more fuel and compete with the short, concentrated deployments preferred by advocates of coastal denial.
COLDWAR_SYR_navy_02.reference: PER_irgc_marines, main MD 05_iran.txt, cost 5.72: convoy escort efficiency +10%, convoy retreat speed +10%, invasion preparation -15%. Syrian escort adaptation uses escort efficiency +10%, naval speed +3%, navy fuel consumption +3%; no allied convoy access or ships are forced.
